prompt:
Create ONE finished, flat, opaque landscape 16:9 event poster for adult neighborhood residents, for a community cultural space and digital screens. Use a clean open editorial arrangement that lets people observe architecture and sunlight at two distances, with approachable exhibition-and-space-talk information. 요청한 화면 비율을 유지하면서 현재 도구와 모델이 지원하는 가능한 최대 해상도로 출력.

Visual system: one continuous pale blue-gray background, dark ink-colored modern Korean editorial sans-serif, a restrained warm orange Korean title. Smooth precise layout, natural photographic contrast, no paper grain, tape, collage adhesive, newspaper effects, installation/mockup, ornamental loops, logos, QR, watermark, invented text or tiny pseudo-print.

Substantive imagery: exactly two sharp architectural photographs embedded within this single poster, different sizes and viewing distances. The large upper-left photo shows a new fictional modest empty interior, an unbranded deep rectangular window opening, thick warm-white plaster reveals, a simple pale stone sill and floor, long sunlight and angular shadow. Photograph the room at a calm wide angle that makes the window depth and light boundary observable. The smaller center-right close-up studies THE SAME sill/reveal and light-shadow boundary from closer: preserve matching orientation, wall/sill materials and light direction so the relationship is visually concrete. It is a near observation of the shared space, not before/after, and not an unrelated second building. No identifiable real architecture or institution; no people, text, branding or signage within the photographs. Plain sharp rectangular photograph edges, no frames or drop shadows.

Composition guide in proportions of the full 16:9 canvas: roomy outer margins about 3.5%. Large room photo upper left, spanning about 46% width and 49% height. Align its left edge with the title below it. Below the photo put a bold orange Korean title on one line, approximately 38px in a 720px-wide QA display; below that, a compact identification group of English name and Korean event description at 19px. On the right, start the date and time at the same top level as the large photograph, around 54% across, bold 26px at a 720px-wide display. Below the schedule, around 34% down, place a smaller close-up photo around 18% width by 23% height, and immediately beside its right edge place the venue and admission text at a readable 18px. Leave enough width for the complete venue on one line. Under this photo-and-venue row, resume one right-column starting edge for the free/interpretation and registration/capacity group at 19px, then a separate welcoming visit group at 18px. Date → venue/admission → free/registration → visit/welcome must be easy to find down the right half. The close-up cannot interrupt this information path. Large photo → lower-left title/event group and upper-right schedule form a balanced diagonal. This is a distributed editorial page, not identical photograph cells or a full-bleed photo with overlaid text.

Print ONLY these eleven entries, each exactly once, preserving spelling, word spaces, punctuation and letter case. Render all as real crisp readable typography; do not condense Hangul or shrink practical information into microcaptions. Each entry stays on a single line; labels in the following production grouping are NOT printed:
Lower-left title:
빛이 머무는 집
Identification group below title:
OPEN HOUSE
건축 사진전 · 공간 이야기
Upper-right schedule:
2027.02.06 토요일
13:00–15:00
Beside close-up, venue and entry:
연남 생활문화공간
12:40부터 입장
Right-column participation group:
관람 무료 · 해설 제공
사전 신청 · 정원 24명
Right-column visit and welcome group:
편한 신발로 방문해 주세요
건축을 몰라도 괜찮아요

The time range has a clearly legible en dash, with intact colons; the separators in the Korean entries are centered middle dots. Even the smallest practical entries need strong contrast and comfortable Korean counters and spacing at 720px-wide viewing. Use one coherent sans-serif family and role-based weight/size hierarchy. Keep the photography observational and inviting rather than luxury real-estate advertising. Deliver only this single complete poster image, not multiple poster alternatives, a contact sheet, a mockup, a photographed print or a stretched/cropped portrait.
